scope: Theorem 6.1 (Four-point voltage convergence) of the manuscript “Spectral convergence for critical FK–Ising planar maps” (preprints/Spectral-convergence-for-critical-FK-Ising-planar-maps-October-5-2026/spectral-convergence-critical-fk-ising-planar-maps.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eeb5895c7058765f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a joint extraction on which Propo- sition 2.4, Theorem 4.2, and Theorem 5.2 hold. Let an, bn, cn, dn be vertex sequences whose canonical positions converge respectively to four pairwise distinct points x, y, z, z0. Normalize the solution of (6.1) by un(dn) = 0. Then, for every compact K ⊂ S2 \ {x, y}, sup v: zn(v)∈K |un(v) − Ux,y;z0 (zn(v))| −→ 0. (6.5) An empty supremum in (6.5) is assigned the value zero. In particular, un(cn) − un(dn) −→ 1 2π log ch(z, y) ch(z0, x) ch(z, x) ch(z0, y) . The assertion holds for any such varying vertex sequences on the extracted sample.
